info.name: Backend AI API
info.description:
Generated from the current apps/api NestJS backend. Global prefix is `/api/v1` (except `health`, which is *supposed* to be excluded but isn't — see the note on the Health Check request). Domains: `health-check`, `example` (generic CRUD reference template — real fields are literally `name`/`col1`/`col2`/`col3`), `auth` (real: `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/login`), and `student` (real: `GET /students` with status/course/search filters, `POST /students`, `PUT /students/:id` — name is immutable on update, see the Update Student request's description).

Known bug (see CLAUDE.md): both `HealthCheckController` and `ExampleController` use bare `@Controller()` with argument-less `@Get()` handlers, so both resolve to `GET /api/v1`. Because `HealthCheckModule` is imported before `ExampleModule` in `app.module.ts`, the health check handler wins and `ExampleController.getAll` is currently unreachable through the HTTP layer.

Separate known issue: errors thrown inside a domain service (e.g. `auth`'s duplicate-email `ConflictException`) don't go through the documented Express-level `errorHandler` — Nest's own exception pipeline intercepts them first, so the response shape for those is `{statusCode, message}` (2 keys), not the `{status, message, error}` (3 keys) shape the rest of the API uses. Both are shown as example responses on the Register request below.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/auth. Password rules (min 8 chars, uppercase, number, special char) are enforced server-side via Joi and mirror the frontend's Zod schema in apps/web/src/modules/onboarding/components/create-account/schema.ts.

request.description: Change {{registerEmail}} (collection variable) before re-running — the email column has a unique index, so re-submitting the same address hits the 409 example below instead of creating a new account.

response.name: 201 Created
409 Conflict (duplicate email — see collection description)
400 Bad Request (weak password)

request.description: Wrong password and unknown email both return the exact same 401 message — deliberate, to avoid leaking which emails are registered. Copy the `token` from a 200 response into the collection's `token` variable to use the Bearer-auth requests elsewhere (note: authenticate.middleware.ts isn't wired to any route yet, so no endpoint actually checks it today).

response.name: 200 OK
401 Unauthorized (wrong password OR unknown email — identical either way)
401 Unauthorized (missing field — validateLogin never returns 400)

item.name: Students
item.description:
Real domain — apps/api/src/domains/student. Every field is required on create, matching the frontend Add Student form. `course` must be one of the fixed course list (apps/api/src/domains/student/constants/courses.constants.ts) or Joi rejects it with 400. Deactivate/activate is `PATCH /students/:id/status` (body `{status: 'active'|'deactivated'}`); delete is a soft-delete via `DELETE /students/:id` (sets status to 'deleted', row stays queryable). Both 404 on an id that's already `deleted` — their existence check deliberately excludes deleted students, same as PUT.

Note for List Students / Get Student by ID: these routes only work because StudentModule is registered before ExampleModule in app.module.ts — ExampleController's bare @Controller() + @Get(':id') greedily matches ANY GET /api/v1/<one-segment> path, so it would otherwise swallow the list request first (same root cause as the health/example collision CLAUDE.md documents). Get Student by ID isn't affected by that collision itself (its path has two segments, `/students/:id`), but it depends on the same registration order to reach StudentController at all. If a future domain's route mysteriously 500s with a uuid-cast error, check module registration order before anything else.

query.description: active | deactivated | deleted — defaults to active if omitted
Comma-separated course names, or repeat the param (?course=A&course=B)
Matches first name, last name, or email

request.description: All three query params are optional and independent — combine any subset. Remove the ones you don't need from the Params tab rather than leaving them empty, since an empty search='' still runs (harmlessly matches everything).

request.description:
IMPORTANT: {{studentDbId}} must be the `id` field (a UUID) from a Create/Update Student response — NOT the human-readable `studentId` (e.g. STU-2401). Sending the wrong one used to 500; it now 400s with a message telling you exactly this, see the example below.

firstName/lastName are deliberately not accepted here — a student's name is immutable after enrollment. Sending them anyway is silently ignored (validate() strips unknown keys before the controller ever sees them); this was verified directly, not just documented.

request.description: Intended route is GET /health (see main.ts's `exclude: ['health']` and startup log line), but the exclude never matches because HealthCheckController's computed path is '' not 'health'. With the global prefix applied it actually lands on GET /api/v1, same as ExampleController.getAll — this request hits the real, currently-working path.
Kept here so this collection stops 404ing the moment the routing bug in CLAUDE.md's 'Known pre-existing bugs' section is fixed — delete once that lands.

request.description: Maps to ExampleController.getAll — but see the collection-level note: this path is currently shadowed by the Health Check handler and won't actually reach this controller until the routing collision is fixed.
